title: AbbVie Gets USFDA Nod for Rinvoq as First Systemic Treatment for Nonsegmental Vitiligo

contentHtml:
New Delhi: AbbVie has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved RINVOQ (upadacitinib;15 mg, once daily) for the treatment of adults and paediatric patients aged 12 years and older with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV), the most common form of vitiligo, often characterised by symmetrical patches of depigmented skin.

RINVOQ, an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, is the first and only FDA-approved systemic therapy for nonsegmental vitiligo in the US.

"The approval of RINVOQ represents an important milestone for people living with nonsegmental vitiligo, providing the first FDA-approved systemic treatment option for this immune-mediated disease," said Roopal Thakkar, executive vice president, research and development, and chief scientific officer at AbbVie.

He added that RINVOQ targets an underlying immune pathway involved in the disease, translating years of research into a new treatment option for patients.

FDA Approval Supported by Phase 3 Viti-Up Clinical Trial Results

The FDA approval is supported by data from the Phase 3 Viti-Up clinical programme, which included two replicate, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind studies evaluating the efficacy and safety of RINVOQ in adults and adolescent patients with nonsegmental vitiligo.

Results showed that significantly more patients treated with RINVOQ 15 mg achieved clinically meaningful improvements in facial repigmentation (F-VASI 75) and total body repigmentation (T-VASI 50) at week 48 compared with patients receiving placebo.

Significantly more patients treated with RINVOQ also achieved F-VASI 90 at week 48. The response rates were 16% and 12% for RINVOQ 15 mg in Viti-Up-1 and Viti-Up-2, respectively, compared with 2% and 3% for placebo.

Further improvements in repigmentation were observed at week 76 among patients who continued treatment with RINVOQ 15 mg during the open-label extension period, with a higher proportion achieving F-VASI 75 and T-VASI 50.

"Nonsegmental vitiligo is a chronic, unpredictable autoimmune disease with a burden that extends well beyond visible pigment loss, affecting patients physically and emotionally. Treatment has historically focused on individual areas of depigmentation rather than addressing the disease more broadly," said Seemal R. Desai, M.D., FAAD, president of the Global Vitiligo Foundation, founder of Innovative Dermatology, Dallas, Texas, and Viti-Up trial investigator. "The Viti-Up clinical program is particularly impactful because it demonstrates the potential of a systemic treatment to achieve robust facial and total body repigmentation. We know that repigmentation takes time, and the significant improvements observed at week 76, with facial and total body response rates doubling or nearly doubling from week 48, are especially encouraging and reinforce the value of a treatment approach that targets the disease from within."

The safety profile of RINVOQ in both Viti-Up studies was generally consistent with that observed in approved indications.1

A New Systemic Option for Nonsegmental Vitiligo, a Chronic, Unpredictable Autoimmune DiseaseVitiligo is a chronic, autoimmune disease that targets the cells responsible for skin pigmentation.4 This unpredictable disease affects nearly 3 million adults in the U.S. and is an autoimmune disease that targets melanocytes, the cells responsible for skin pigmentation.4 The disease can unexpectedly progress, even after long periods of stability, making early disease control an important treatment goal.5,6 Because repigmentation can take months, long-term systemic treatment options are important for people living with nonsegmental vitiligo.4,7

"For the vitiligo community, approval of the first systemic treatment option for nonsegmental vitiligo is an important development in advancing care," said Richard Huggins, M.D., board member of the Global Vitiligo Foundation. "This approval reflects growing recognition of vitiligo as a serious autoimmune disease and the true burden it places on those living with the condition. For many in the vitiligo community, this approval represents a significant step forward in the treatment landscape."

Viti-Up Clinical Trials

Viti-Up is a clinical program with a single protocol encompassing two replicate, independent Phase 3 studies (Viti-Up-1 and Viti-Up-2). The trials were designed to evaluate the efficacy, safety and tolerability of RINVOQ 15 mg in adult and adolescent patients (ages 12 and older) living with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who were eligible for systemic therapy. In both studies, patients received RINVOQ 15 mg once daily or placebo. Both studies included a 48-week placebo-controlled, double-blind treatment period (period A) and a 112-week open-label extension period (period B). The co-primary endpoints were the achievements of ≥75% repigmentation of facial vitiligo (F-VASI 75) and ≥50% repigmentation of total body vitiligo (T-VASI 50) from baseline at week 48. More information on these trials can be found at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06118411).

RINVOQ® (upadacitinib)

Discovered and developed by AbbVie scientists, RINVOQ is a selective JAK inhibitor that is being studied in several immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. Based on enzymatic and cellular assays, RINVOQ demonstrated greater inhibitory potency for JAK-1 vs JAK-2, JAK-3, and TYK-2. The relevance of inhibition of specific JAK enzymes to therapeutic effectiveness and safety is not currently known.

RINVOQ treats several immune-mediated inflammatory diseases and is currently approved in the U.S. for 10 indications across various immune-mediated, inflammatory diseases and is being studied in Phase 3 clinical trials for alopecia areata, hidradenitis suppurativa, Takayasu arteritis and systemic lupus erythematosus. The additional approvals for RINVOQ use reflect AbbVie's continued research beyond the first indication, which has helped bring more approved treatments to patient populations, including some with significant unmet needs.

RINVOQ (upadacitinib) U.S. Uses and Important Safety Information

RINVOQ is a prescription medicine used to treat:

  • Adults with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) when 1 or more medicines called tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blockers have been used, and did not work well or could not be tolerated.
  • Adults with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA) when 1 or more medicines called TNF blockers have been used, and did not work well or could not be tolerated.
  • Adults with active ankylosing spondylitis (AS) when 1 or more medicines called TNF blockers have been used, and did not work well or could not be tolerated.
  • Adults with active non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA) with objective signs of inflammation when a TNF blocker medicine has been used, and did not work well or could not be tolerated.
  • Adults with giant cell arteritis (GCA).
  • Adults with moderate to severe ulcerative colitis (UC) when 1 or more medicines called TNF blockers have been used and did not work well or could not be tolerated, or after taking a different injection or pill (systemic therapy) when your healthcare provider does not recommend TNF blockers.
  • Adults with moderate to severe Crohn's disease (CD) when 1 or more medicines called TNF blockers have been used and did not work well or could not be tolerated, or after taking a different injection or pill (systemic therapy) when your healthcare provider does not recommend TNF blockers.

It is not known if RINVOQ is safe and effective in children with ankylosing spondylitis, non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease.

  • Adults and children 12 years of age and older with moderate to severe eczema (atopic dermatitis [AD]) that did not respond to previous treatment and their eczema is not well controlled with other pills or injections, including biologic medicines, or the use of other pills or injections is not recommended.
  • Adults and children 12 years of age and older with a type of vitiligo called nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV).

It is not known if RINVOQ is safe and effective in children under 12 years of age with atopic dermatitis or nonsegmental vitiligo.

It is not known if RINVOQ LQ is safe and effective in children with atopic dermatitis or nonsegmental vitiligo.

RINVOQ/RINVOQ LQ is a prescription medicine used to treat:

  • Children 2 years of age and older with active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pJIA) when 1 or more medicines called TNF blockers have been used, and did not work well or could not be tolerated.
  • Children 2 to less than 18 years of age with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA) when 1 or more medicines called TNF blockers have been used, and did not work well or could not be tolerated.

It is not known if RINVOQ/RINVOQ LQ is safe and effective in children under 2 years of age with polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis or psoriatic arthritis.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION FOR RINVOQ/RINVOQ LQ (upadacitinib)

What is the most important information one should know about RINVOQ*?

RINVOQ may cause serious side effects, including:

  • Serious infections. RINVOQ can lower your ability to fight infections. Serious infections have happened while taking RINVOQ, including tuberculosis (TB) and infections caused by bacteria, fungi, or viruses that can spread throughout the body. Some people have died from these infections. Your healthcare provider (HCP) should test you for TB before starting RINVOQ and check you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during treatment with RINVOQ. You should not start taking RINVOQ if you have any kind of infection unless your HCP tells you it is okay. If you get a serious infection, your HCP may stop your treatment until your infection is controlled. You may be at higher risk of developing shingles (herpes zoster).
  • Increased risk of death in people 50 years and older who have at least 1 heart disease (cardiovascular) risk factor.
  • Cancer and immune system problems. RINVOQ may increase your risk of certain cancers. Lymphoma and other cancers, including skin cancers, can happen. Current or past smokers are at higher risk of certain cancers, including lymphoma and lung cancer. Follow your HCP's advice about having your skin checked for skin cancer during treatment with RINVOQ. Limit the amount of time you spend in sunlight. Wear protective clothing when you are in the sun and use sunscreen.
  • Increased risk of major cardiovascular (CV) events, such as heart attack, stroke, or death, in people 50 years and older who have at least 1 heart disease (CV) risk factor, especially if you are a current or past smoker.
  • Blood clots. Blood clots in the veins of the legs or lungs and arteries can happen with RINVOQ. This may be life-threatening and cause death. Blood clots in the veins of the legs and lungs have happened more often in people who are 50 years and older and with at least 1 heart disease (CV) risk factor. Blood clots can also form in the veins of the brain.
  • Allergic reactions. Symptoms such as rash (hives), trouble breathing, feeling faint or dizzy, or swelling of your lips, tongue, or throat, which may mean you are having an allergic reaction, have been seen in people taking RINVOQ. Some of these reactions were serious. If any of these symptoms occur during treatment with RINVOQ, stop taking RINVOQ and get emergency medical help right away.
  • Tears in the stomach or intestines. This happens most often in people who take nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or corticosteroids. Get medical help right away if you get stomach-area pain, fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting.
  • Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) in people with diabetes. If you have diabetes, your HCP may tell you to check your blood sugar (glucose) more often during treatment with RINVOQ. Call your HCP if you have any problems with low blood sugar.
  • Changes in certain laboratory tests. Your HCP should do blood tests before you start taking RINVOQ and while you take it. Your HCP may stop your RINVOQ treatment for a period of time if needed because of changes in these blood test results.

RINVOQ should not be taken by people allergic to upadacitinib or any of its ingredients.

Precautions Before Starting Treatment

Patients should inform their healthcare providers if they:

Have an active infection, recurrent infections or symptoms of infection, including fever, chills, cough, shortness of breath, muscle aches or unexplained weight loss; Have tuberculosis or have been in close contact with someone who has TB; Are current or former smokers; Have a history of heart attack, other heart problems or stroke; Have or have had cancer, hepatitis B or C, shingles, blood clots, diverticulitis or stomach or intestinal ulcers; Have liver problems, diabetes, low blood cell counts, chronic lung disease, HIV or a weakened immune system; Live in or have travelled to areas where certain fungal infections are more common, including the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys and the Southwest; Have recently received or are scheduled to receive a vaccine. Live vaccines should be avoided during treatment.

Women who are pregnant or planning pregnancy should discuss the potential risks with their healthcare provider. Based on animal studies, RINVOQ may harm an unborn baby. Effective contraception is recommended during treatment and for four weeks after the last dose.

A pregnancy surveillance programme is available for patients who become pregnant while taking RINVOQ. They are encouraged to report pregnancies by calling 1-800-633-9110.

Patients should not breastfeed during treatment or for six days after the last dose, as RINVOQ may pass into breast milk.

Patients should also inform their healthcare providers about all prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal supplements they are taking. Particular attention should be given to medicines used to treat fungal or bacterial infections, rifampicin, phenytoin and medicines that affect the immune system.

Patients should avoid food and drinks containing grapefruit while taking RINVOQ, as grapefruit may increase the risk of side effects.

Monitoring During Treatment

Patients should immediately inform their healthcare providers if they develop symptoms of infection, as RINVOQ may increase susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections.

Emergency medical attention is required if symptoms of a heart attack or stroke occur, including:

Chest discomfort or severe chest pain; Shortness of breath; Cold sweats, nausea or vomiting; Light-headedness; Sudden weakness on one side of the body; Slurred speech.

Patients should stop taking RINVOQ and seek immediate medical attention if they experience symptoms of blood clots, including:

Swelling, redness, weakness or numbness in an arm or leg; Pain or tenderness in one or both legs; A new, unusual or severe headache; Difficulty speaking, drowsiness or confusion; Sudden unexplained chest or upper back pain; Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing; Blurred vision, double vision or loss of vision.

Patients should also inform their healthcare providers if they develop persistent fever, abdominal pain or changes in bowel habits.

Other Possible Side Effects

Common side effects of RINVOQ include upper respiratory tract infections, shingles, herpes simplex infections, bronchitis, nausea, cough, fever, acne, headache, peripheral oedema, increased creatine phosphokinase levels, allergic reactions, folliculitis, abdominal pain, weight gain, influenza, fatigue, reduced white blood cell counts, muscle pain, flu-like illness, rash, increased cholesterol and other blood fats, elevated liver enzyme levels, pneumonia, anaemia and gastroenteritis.

Retinal detachment has also been reported in patients with atopic dermatitis treated with RINVOQ. Patients should contact their healthcare providers immediately if they experience sudden changes in vision.

Some patients may notice medicine residue, including a whole tablet or tablet pieces, in their stool. They should contact their healthcare provider if this occurs.

These are not all the possible side effects of RINVOQ.

Dosage and Administration

RINVOQ tablets are taken once daily, with or without food, as directed by a healthcare provider. Tablets should not be split, crushed or chewed.

The medicine is available in 15 mg, 30 mg and 45 mg extended-release tablets.

RINVOQ LQ is an oral solution available at a concentration of 1 mg/mL and is taken twice daily, with or without food. RINVOQ LQ is not the same as RINVOQ tablets. Patients should not switch between the two formulations unless directed by their healthcare provider.

Unless otherwise stated, the safety information for RINVOQ also applies to RINVOQ LQ.

Patients should consult their healthcare providers for complete prescribing information. Adverse events associated with prescription medicines can be reported to the FDA. AbbVie may also provide assistance to patients experiencing difficulty paying for their medicines.

Prescribing information varies by country, and patients and healthcare professionals should refer to the applicable local product label.

AbbVie is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing medicines for serious health conditions. Its key therapeutic areas include immunology, neuroscience and oncology, alongside products and services in its Allergan Aesthetics portfolio.

The company reports that more than one million patients worldwide are treated with its immunology medicines, which are approved in more than 175 countries across over 20 immune-mediated diseases affecting adults and children.
